title: Runtime Access Quantizer and Authorization Decision Bus for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a pluggable, low-latency policy evaluation engine (the Decision Bus) and a lightweight authorization middleware (the Quantizer) that together provide consistent RBAC v2 enforcement across API, runtime, and Console surfaces. This ticket covers: 1) a compact, cache-friendly evaluator with permissive failover semantics; 2) a middleware shim for API/runtime that applies decisions, emits structured audit events, and integrates SSO/SAML identity assertions; 3) admin controls and debug endpoints for safe rollouts. The implementation must be deployable in hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes and respect tenant isolation and KMS-backed signing for audit integrity.
acceptance_criteria: Decision Bus implements a policy evaluation API compatible with existing authz adapters and returns decisions in <10ms p50 for cached paths
Quantizer middleware applies allow/deny/conditional decisions and exposes a lightweight explain() header for Developer Console requests
All authorization decisions produce structured audit events sent to the audit pipeline with request context, identity markers (SSO subject, SAML attributes), and decision provenance
Canary rollout plan executed: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on error rate regressions
Security review completed and signed-off by Security team (SAML threat model, replay protection, audit integrity)
Integration tests cover policy changes, tenant-scoped policies, and fallback-to-legacy-authorizer behavior
Admins can revoke cached decisions via API and see last-eval traces in Console (RBAC admin page)
technical_design: High level: introduce a thin Decision Bus service that evaluates RBAC v2 policies (PL/JSON or compiled rule trie) with an inner LRU eval cache keyed by (tenant, subject-hash, resource, action, prefix-hash). The Quantizer middleware will run in-process for low-latency paths and call the Decision Bus for cache misses or non-cached tenants. To support Private deployments we provide a sidecar binary that exposes the same in-process shim.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: in-process caching improves latency but increases per-instance memory. We limit cache size and provide eviction/metrics per tenant.
Fail-open vs fail-closed: default is fail-open for read-only endpoints and fail-closed for admin-sensitive endpoints. This is configurable per-route via annotations.
Policy format: initially support a superset of existing RBAC v1 rule objects to simplify migration; compile hot paths into decision tries for speed.
Audit volume: emitting detailed explain traces increases cost — provide sampling controls and 'full-audit' mode for compliance tenants.
tasks: Design: policy trie schema and cache key format
Prototype: in-memory Decision Bus with eval cache
Middleware: Quantizer shim for HTTP/gRPC interceptors
SAML integration: accept and normalize SAML attributes into subject claims
Audit: structured event schema + pipeline hooks to existing audit streamer
Console: admin UI for decision trace lookup and cache invalidation
Testing: unit, integration, load test for p95/p99 latency
Rollout: canary scripts and observability dashboards
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting — aligned on cache key and fallthrough semantics. Action: engineering to draft trie schema (owner: Liam).
2026-03-04: Prototype Decision Bus implemented (in-memory) with basic allow/deny evaluation. P50 cache hit path ~6ms locally.
2026-03-06: Middleware shim scaffold completed for HTTP interceptors. Initial integration tests pass for simple policies.
2026-03-08: Security provided preliminary SAML attribute mapping guidance; replay protection and signature verification delegated to SSO layer, Decision Bus will accept validated identity tokens.
2026-03-10: Performance tuning — reduced allocations in trie walker, added metrics for cache hit/miss and eval duration. Preparing RFC for Console admin UI design.
implementation_notes: Default decision event includes: timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, subject_id, subject_source (SSO provider), policy_version, rule_id, decision, reason_code, eval_latency_ms. For private installs, decision signing uses KMS/HSM via existing envelope encryption integrations. Ensure cross-tenant policy leaks are impossible by scoping caches and indices by tenant_id.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for policy compiler and trie walker. 2) Integration tests with sso-saml-normalizer asserting correct subject mapping. 3) Load test: simulate 10k RPS with 95/5 cache hit/miss and confirm 99th percentile <50ms. 4) Canary: enable Quantizer for non-admin routes in a small percentage of production traffic and monitor error budget and audit event volume.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: internal dev deploy. Stage 1: small canary (1%) for low-risk routes with full audit sampling; monitor for 24 hours. Stage 2: increase to 10% and enable admin trace feature for staging tenants. Stage 3: 50% if stable. Stage 4: full rollout. Rollback triggers: >0.5% increase in 5xx or >10% CPU spike vs baseline or audit pipeline backlog exceeding threshold.
risks: Audit pipeline could be overwhelmed by verbose traces — mitigate with sampling controls and backpressure signals
Cache poisoning across tenants if keys are not correctly namespaced
SAML attribute permutations could produce inconsistent subject identities across providers — require canonicalization via sso-saml-normalizer
